nested_lists.name: encroachments_or_overlaps
nested_lists.shape_reason: encroachments genuinely repeat and are the single most decision-relevant recurring finding on a survey (they can block clear title/marketability); a flat row (description + affected boundary + location) keeps well under the 16,384-token ceiling; serves processor review (no rule yet). One list only per the token budget

encoding_variations: Surveyor credential appears as 'PLS 12345,' 'RLS 12345,' or 'License No. 12345' and the state may be separate — surveyor_license_state is the disambiguator
Area is stated in acres and/or square feet ('0.34 AC / 14,810 SF') — capture verbatim as a string
Flood zone on a survey references a FEMA panel number and effective date; keep the panel with the zone

open_questions.q: Which findings list gets the one nested-list slot: encroachments vs easements? Both repeat and both matter for title.
options: encroachments (drafted) — they most often trigger conditions
easements — more numerous, affect lien priority
a single merged survey_exceptions list with a finding_type column
open_questions.recommendation: a single merged survey_exceptions list if a survey-findings rule is ever built; encroachments-only for now GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: surveyor_certification_text length — the certification block can be long.
open_questions.recommendation: full text — processors need the exact 'certified to' parties and a rule cannot re-derive them from a summary

notes: No rules read this document today (rule_count 0); there is no rule floor. A boundary/ALTA survey is findings-heavy; most detail lists have no consumer and stay in the catch-all. Fields earn a place by identity, disambiguation, or processor use.
No restricted fields on this doc. Names are standard sensitivity -> identity fields, not registry PII. No _PII_FIELDS additions.
